newsitem.title: GERMANY: German wheat steadier, sellers tighten supply.
newsitem.headline: German wheat steadier, sellers tighten supply.

text.p: German wheat prices have been marked up in thin trade following the four-day Easter holiday, brokers said on Wednesday.
"Sellers are holding back with offers because they are confident more business will develop after recent sales," one said.
"April buyers may soon be looking for spring and summer supply ahead of the 1997 harvest."
The Hamburg grain exchange this week raised its spot bread wheat price (12.5 percent, 220 Hagberg) by 2.50 marks to 280 marks a tonne free Hamburg and the spot feed wheat price also rose 2.50 to 275.
Fob Baltic sellers left first half April delivery 12 percent protein wheat at 280-295 marks, the level seen over the past three weeks.
First half April material with 13/14 percent protein was in a broadly unchanged 287.50-309 marks range, with top grades boosted by southern European milling industry demand for blending.
Fob Baltic barley was unchanged at 262.50-282.50 marks, depending on shipment sizes, amid muted demand.
Fob rye sellers were also steady at 262-272 marks.
While feed rye continued to be offered into intervention, sellers of bread varieties were keeping prices up in the hope for EU export allocations to third countries.
Eastern German bread rye sellers reported some sales to Austria and the Czech republic.
The April intervention buying-in price for all grains is 245.83 marks.
